verdict.rationale: Browserbase's own docs describe programmatic browser sessions with full control, and agents that log in, fill forms and pass login walls to pull data, so the core interact-and-authenticate flow is first-party. The docs do not explicitly show continuing interaction on the same page or session after a scrape or fetch: the URL-fetch product is described separately from interactive sessions. missing for 10: explicit documentation of persisting or continuing a session from an already-scraped page, concrete click and form-fill API examples, independent or hands-on corroboration of authenticated scraping.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep interacting with an already-scraped page, clicking and filling forms to reach content behind a login wall

citations.quote: Create, control, and observe browser sessions programmatically.
Full browser control with auto-waits, network interception, and multi-tab support.
Your agent logs in, navigates, and pulls data from any website, login walls included.
When your workflow requires a form, a CAPTCHA, or a login prompt, it's handled.
